correctness.rationale: For 64 indices the first frame analyzes \(e_1\) at scale \(1/2\), and on the next 64 it analyzes \(e_2\); the second family swaps these directions, giving both tight frame bounds \(64/4=16\). The choices \(\lambda_1=\lambda_2=1/100\) and \(\mu=3/4\) make the published scalar smallness expression \(83/100<1\). For all coefficients the norm of separate adjoint differences is \(\|c_{\rm act}\|/\sqrt2\le\mu\|c\|\), whereas the actual synthesis-difference norm is \(8\). Taking the first frame on indices 1--64 and the second frame on 65--128 repeats only the \(e_1\) functional, so this weave annihilates \(e_2\). This directly contradicts the claimed lower bound \(8\), without any limit or numerical approximation. The exact source theorem and the invalid norm substitution in its proof were directly inspected in the primary publisher PDF.

final_claim: Theorem 2.4 of Rajput--Sahu--Mishra (2021) is false as printed: there are two tight scalar \(g\)-frames in \(\mathbb C^2\), each with bounds \(16\), satisfying the published componentwise perturbation inequality and scalar smallness condition but admitting a weave with zero lower frame bound.
